title: Erasmian Koine Greek alphabet — app clip pack
notes: Each clip is name then sound. Master file inserts 1.60s silence between clips for easy snipping. Cue times are for the master file. Two rows were regenerated later and are not in the master: they carry source, take and a note instead of master offsets. Each row carries a sha1 of its mp3, checked by tools/check_sounds.py, so a clip cannot be replaced without the record of what was spoken moving with it.

clips.name: Zeta
clips.note: The pack's /dz/ never came out. 'Italian za' gave dizzah, a disyllable. 'zuh' gives a clean /z/, which is what two thirds of the word clips already say — so the clip agrees with the deck and diverges from the teaching, which stays Black's [dz]. Judged by ear, Fraser.

clips.name: Eta
clips.note: Cued 'ay', which Atlas read as /aI/ — English 'ay' is ambiguous, say against aye — so the clip said 'eye' where Black gives obey. Its name was judged fine, so only the sound is replaced: the /eI/ of a take of 'eigh', cut at 0.385 s, before the g the generator marks at 0.39 and Fraser heard. Judged by ear, Fraser.

clips.name: Theta
clips.note: Cued 'th' and it spoke the word 'thin'. That is Black's own keyword, so it was not wrong — but every other letter clip gives a sound, not a word. Recued 'Theta.  Thh.' in one take. Its sound measured 19.5 dB below its own name, which is the nature of a voiceless dental fricative rather than a bad take, so that half was lifted 10 dB. Judged by ear, Fraser.

clips.name: Xi
clips.note: Neither half could be generated. The shipped clip was heard as 'she' with a /k/ for its sound; every name cue Atlas was given — ksee, ksi, xee, ksigh, Xi — was spelled out as X-I. The Greek name xi, sent as Greek across all 28 voices, is said correctly but as /ksi/, and this course names its letters in English: Pi and Psi both measure as /aI/ diphthongs, so /ksi/ would leave xi the odd letter out. So the clip is assembled: the name is the /ks/ of 'axe' crossfaded onto the /aI/ vowel of 16_pi.mp3, and the sound is that same 'axe' /ks/ again, cut at the x anchor the generator itself reported. Gap and timing follow 16_pi. All Atlas, one voice. Judged by ear, Fraser.

clips.name: Pi
clips.note: The shipped clip said 'hi'. It had no plosive release at all: from 0.186 s a 60 ms aspiration ramp — 22, 41, 57, 79, 96, 114 — climbing into voicing, where a /p/ is silence then a sharp transient. Cued 'Pie.  Puh.' in one take; word-initial /p/ is ordinary in English, so unlike psi and xi this needed no splice. Split at the generator's own character marks and re-spaced to the pack's 0.18 / 0.355 / 0.28. Judged by ear, Fraser.

clips.name: Upsilon
clips.note: Two faults in one clip, and the second was only found by looking. Fraser heard the NAME as "up silon" and asked for "oop silon": every other letter here opens on its own sound -- EP-silon, OM-icron, AY-ta -- and lesson 1 teaches upsilon as "u as in lute / put", cued oo. Standard English really does say UP-silon, so this is a teaching choice and not a correction. And the SOUND half was recorded as "ew / ue", a value the cue guide overruled long ago -- the pack is consistent that upsilon is oo -- so the sheet had been describing a sound the course does not teach. His verdict was the name from the shipped clip and the sound from a take of 'Oop silon.  Ooh.' -- Ooh and not oo, because bare oo was read out as letters when d08_ou was fixed. So this is a splice, the method eta, ei and xi were all repaired by: cut in the silence either side with 10-30ms fades, re-spaced to lead 0.19 / gap 0.39 / tail 0.29 against pi's 0.16 / 0.35 / 0.26. One thing improved by accident: the old clip peaked at -9.7 dB, louder than every other letter, and this one is -13.6 where pi and epsilon sit. Judged by ear, Fraser.

clips.name: Chi
clips.note: Both halves were rejected: the name came out with the soft ch of 'church' instead of /kaI/, and the sound came out as the WORD 'Bach'. Recued 'Kai.  Khh.' in one take, sound half lifted 5 dB. This clip settles what chi is: its sound measures 260 ms of sustained energy at zero-crossing 0.22-0.28, which is frication, not the burst-plus-tail of an aspirated stop. So it is the loch sound lesson 1 teaches, and chi stays a declared departure from Black's 'chemist'. Judged by ear, Fraser.

clips.name: Psi
clips.note: Atlas will say the NAME psi with its p, and will not say the bare cluster: English has no word-initial /ps/, so there is nothing in the voice's experience to produce. The second half is therefore not spoken at all — it is the first 160 ms of this clip's own name, cut at the vowel and faded. Splicing from the deck's psuche was tried first and failed: that clip has NO plosive release, energy climbing smoothly out of silence into frication, so there was never a /p/ in it to lift. Fraser heard that before it was measured. Judged by ear, Fraser.

clips.name: epsilon + iota
clips.note: The same fault and the same fix as 07_eta: cued 'ay', said 'eye', where Black gives eight. One cue settled both. Judged by ear, Fraser.

clips.name: omicron + upsilon
clips.note: 'oo' was read as letters. 'ooh' gives Black's soup vowel. Judged by ear, Fraser.
